body:
To be concrete: check out e.g.:
- https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-select-setter (select's indexed setter)
- https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-domstringmap-nameditem (DOMStringMap's named getter, followed by its setter and deleter)
- https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-nameditem (Document's named getter, which is different in style than most)

The first two (and others like them) have `<dfn>`s around the IDL terms "determine the value of a named property", "set", and "delete an existing named property" among others. This is very weird to me:
- They are not defining those terms
- A reader is not made aware that these are IDL hooks that have definitions elsewhere which we are overriding

The reason this is done is so that in the IDL, the words `getter`/`setter`/`deleter` have somewhere to link to (which is a fairly noble goal).

My suggestion would be that we add `id`s to the paragraphs defining these for the IDL to link to, and then convert them from `<dfn>`s to cross-linking `<span>`s.
